models_skipped.dac_swinl_indoor: eval_baseline_joint.py's DACAdapter.predict_frame raises NotImplementedError('DAC is ERP-native; use predict_erp') by design -- DAC produces an ERP euclidean-range depth + in-FOV mask, not a fisheye/pinhole planar-z map, and model_zoo.py's own comment says the ERP->fisheye inverse remap needed to score it through this evaluator's theta x GT-depth protocol is 'not on the hot path' (i.e. genuinely unimplemented, not a small adapter kwarg). This is the exact 'dac ERP path' case the ticket flagged as acceptable to skip-and-say-so rather than scratch-adapt. Environment-side, DAC itself was made runnable (missing wandb pip dep installed; missing MultiScaleDeformableAttention CUDA extension built after a 2-line .type()->.scalar_type() fix for the current torch API in the vendored third_party/depth_any_camera; config+weights downloaded) -- the blocker is specifically the planar-z/ERP output-format mismatch in the BENCH harness, not weights or environment.

near_rim_definition: count-weighted mean AbsRel over joint-table cells with theta_bin_mid_deg >= 38 and depth row in {0-1m, 1-2m} (<=2m), matching the project's existing near_rim zone convention.
read: dav2_large (relative-depth, scale-shift-per-frame) is a clear outlier on seq136 specifically (whole AbsRel 0.317, d1 0.496) but not on decoration_seq132 (0.089) -- a scene-specific scale-shift failure, not a systematic relative-depth weakness. The three metric models (unik3d_vitl, da3_small on decoration, vggt_omega) are close together on whole-image AbsRel (0.04-0.07); da3_small is notably worse on seq136 specifically (0.138) than its own decoration_seq132 number (0.044), suggesting DA3-Small's own scene sensitivity rather than a universal seq136 difficulty (unik3d/vggt_omega/da3_large don't show the same seq136 penalty). Not tuned toward any paper's target numbers.
